messages.displayText: Welcome to the Lumiose Museum.

We are currently hosting a special exhibition on
the second floor.

The Hisui region?
Never heard of it.

Seems the museum lends their
pieces to far-off regions?

“Farmers and Pokémon”...?
What Pokémon is that?

It lives on forever in art...
its essence captured in paint.

You can find fossils in the
Glittering Cave sometimes.

Ah, I remember that Lucario
statue from the Tower of Mastery!
That’s one big Lucario! Maybe it’s an alpha?

Lucario was the first Pokémon to ever be Mega
Evolved in the Kalos region, right?

This old noble had himself painted
with a rare Pokémon to show off.

Who’s this guy? And
what’s that Pokémon?

A knight on a training
journey with his Golurk, huh?

I’m pooped!
Aren’t you?

That means we had
a proper look around.

Is that house...built
into the tree itself?

It’s a pretty common
sight in Laverre City.

So these aristocrats built unique
castles in their territories, huh...

This must depict those
statues at the Parfum Palace.

It’s a whole series of paintings of power plants in
Kalos. Someone truly loved them, no?

A whole Lumiose City made outta holo-tech?!
This is the coolest thing ever!
Prism Tower really is kinda ginormous, huh?

Sheesh, I didn’t even realize there were this many
different kinds of Poké Balls.

No wonder some people start getting particular
about which ball they use for each Pokémon.

I wonder if anyone’s working
on any new kinds of Poké Balls.

Apparently all this stuff is either
borrowed or modern replicas.

They used to make their
Poké Balls by hand?!

Hisui is an ancient name for a distant region. The
people there greatly feared Pokémon.

It seems that old survey work really led to people
and Pokémon better understanding one another.

They must’ve reconstructed this
based on contemporary records...

They say these Pokémon control
time and space even now.

Dialga and Palkia are Legendary
Pokémon in the Sinnoh region.

I was told that the person who wore this outfit
donated it to the collection personally.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Apparently he gazed a while at those sketches by
Professor Laventon with this nostalgic air, too...

This piece was long believed to have been a
portrait of a king from three thousand years ago,<U+0010><U+0001>븀
painted by an artist who lived after his time.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
However, recent research has lent support to the
theory that this painting in fact depicts a<U+0010><U+0001>븀
descendant of the king’s younger brother.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
From this, we can surmise that this royal line
maintained a degree of power through the ages.

It’s a dark and narrow cave. The source of its
eerie light is a plant called Luminous Moss.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This work is part of a series depicting sceneries
that inspired overseas artists while they were<U+0010><U+0001>븀
traveling in Kalos.

It captures the lives of Pokémon and farmers who
lived together with the land.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It was painted about 85 years ago and is regarded
as an example of naturalism.

The Tower of Mastery stands to the north of
Shalour City.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Two strange stones were once discovered in this
area, which are now thought to have been the<U+0010><U+0001>븀
first known Mega Stone and Key Stone.

The giant Mega Lucario statue that stands within
the Tower of Mastery.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
In order to directly view its face, one must climb
to the second floor of the tower.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Within the base of the statue is a room that only
successors or related personnel can enter.

A depiction of the Fruit Pokémon Tsareena and
the Scarecrow Pokémon Cacturne.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Some have chosen to explore the figures of
Pokémon—so different than humans—in order to<U+0010><U+0001>븀
better understand their anatomy and to explore<U+0010><U+0001>븀
the nature of their hearts and minds.

Pokémon sharing a moment together, centered
around Gothitelle.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Many artists have displayed curiosity about how
Pokémon would relate to each other in the<U+0010><U+0001>븀
absence of humans.

A painting of the Mythical Pokémon Diancie.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The artist boldly eschews painting a background
altogether, keeping the focus solely on Diancie.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Thus, we can feel the artist’s desire to emphasize
that the subject transcends eras and trends.

This is a replica of the Mega Lucario statue in the
Tower of Mastery.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The original statue was created to commemorate
the fact that Lucario was the first Pokémon to<U+0010><U+0001>븀
ever Mega Evolve in the Kalos region.

A shining stone that emitted great warmth was
discovered.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The Tower of Mastery was then built to house and
protect the stone. To this day, the successor to<U+0010><U+0001>븀
Mega Evolution carries on the legend of the<U+0010><U+0001>븀
mysterious stone.

It is said that one only gains their Mega Ring after
defeating the successor to Mega Evolution in a<U+0010><U+0001>븀
Pokémon battle atop the Tower of Mastery.

Only the chosen may climb the Tower of Mastery.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It also requires skill with roller skates to reach the
top floor.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
One must have complete mastery of their own
body to become a Mega Evolution user.

It’s a map of the Lumiose Museum. The grand
exhibition on Hisui is on the second floor.

They say a man of power at the time forced the
artist to add the Mythical Pokémon Mew to<U+0010><U+0001>븀
spread the word of how great he was.

This painting depicts a knight-errant who
continues his travels with a Pokémon, Golurk.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The painting expresses the knight’s identity and
his suffering as its primary subjects.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is regarded as an example of romanticism.

A city that looks like a hideaway for fairies.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A huge tree stands in the center, and the
Pokémon Gym is nestled in the tree.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This work is part of a series depicting sceneries
that inspired overseas artists while they were<U+0010><U+0001>븀
traveling in Kalos.

The courtyard of the Parfum Palace.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A statue that celebrates cooperation between
Pokémon and people stands in the courtyard.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This work is part of a series depicting sceneries
that inspired overseas artists while they were<U+0010><U+0001>븀
traveling in Kalos.

Around the time the Parfum Palace was built,
aristocrats who served the king created unique<U+0010><U+0001>븀
castles in their territories.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This work is highly praised as a piece that
captures that period in time.

This piece is a key work in the rise of the realist
movement.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It depicts with keen accuracy the scenery in an
area near Coumarine City in Kalos.
Replicas of the various Poké Balls in use today.
Replicas of the various Poké Balls in use today.

This factory makes Poké Balls and ships them all
over the Kalos region.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This painting is part of a series on technology in
Kalos, and the ever-increasing number of<U+0010><U+0001>븀
Poké Balls expresses the artist’s desire to be<U+0010><U+0001>븀
connected to all Pokémon.

This power plant uses fire to generate electricity.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This painting is part of a series on technology in
Kalos, and the fierce combustion fully commu-<U+0010><U+0001>븀
nicates the passionate fire of the energy of life.

This plant uses gas from composting waste to
generate electricity.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This painting is part of a series on technology in
Kalos, and it expresses the sorrow of wanting to<U+0010><U+0001>븀
leave some legacy behind, even though we pass<U+0010><U+0001>븀
on and disappear.

This plant uses heat from the ground to
generate electricity.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This painting is part of a series on technology in
Kalos, and the plant is a sharp commentary on<U+0010><U+0001>븀
the hidden passion that lies just beneath<U+0010><U+0001>븀
everyone’s surface.

This plant gathers sunlight in space in order to
generate electricity.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This painting is part of a series on technology in
Kalos, and the artist has succeeded in capturing<U+0010><U+0001>븀
the sense of self-efficacy in the region—of being<U+0010><U+0001>븀
isolated but still striving to help others.

It’s a three-dimensional map of Lumiose City,
created using holo-tech.

Hisui: The Grand Exhibition<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The lands once known as Hisui reveal how
humans and Pokémon came to live in harmony.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
With the help of various museums and collectors,
we bring you all the relics—and some replicas—<U+0010><U+0001>븀
that we can from this fascinating place and time.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
We hope you’ll come away from this exhibit with
a sense of the daily life and customs of Hisui.

Hisui Region Map No. 1<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This map depicts the area around the settlement
of Jubilife, base of the Galaxy Expedition Team.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Many children can be seen, perhaps indicating
that the fear of Pokémon had lessened and life<U+0010><U+0001>븀
had stabilized by this time.

Hisui Region Map No. 2<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This map depicts the Coronet Highlands, as well
as the Crimson Mirelands and Lake Valor.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Though very different from the modern Sinnoh
region, the geography itself is accurately shown.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is believed that the surveyor viewed the area
from above while riding upon a flying Pokémon.

Poké Balls of the Hisui Region<U+0010><U+0001>븁
People of the time crafted their own Poké Balls
using Apricorns and the mineral tumblestone.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Many varieties are said to have been crafted, each
displaying different properties depending on what<U+0010><U+0001>븀
materials were used.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Crafting one’s own Poké Balls in the modern age
would be a true labor of love, given the difficulty.

Sketches Drawn by Professor Laventon<U+0010><U+0001>븁
His original Pokédex was long assumed to be
lost, until a partial facsimile was found in the<U+0010><U+0001>븀
shed of a private house in the Sinnoh region.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This discovery has helped advance the studies of
Professor Laventon and the Pokédex he created.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
His work has been reevaluated in recent years,
with particular appreciation for his accurate<U+0010><U+0001>븀
sketches of Pokémon and his gift for capturing<U+0010><U+0001>븀
Pokémon’s quirks within his skillful descriptions.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is said his Pokédex was not in fact completed by
Laventon himself but by a mysterious, 15-year-old<U+0010><U+0001>븀
youth who appeared out of nowhere one day.

Crafting Bench<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A bench where Galaxy Expedition Team members
would craft Poké Balls and other necessities<U+0010><U+0001>븀
using materials they had gathered.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Crafting benches were set up in various locations,
but there were also portable crafting kits that<U+0010><U+0001>븀
could be utilized wherever the user might be.

Survey Corps Satchel<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A satchel that was supplied to members of the
Galaxy Team Survey Corps.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Should a Survey Corps member be knocked out
while conducting a survey, the Security Corps<U+0010><U+0001>븀
would rescue them and retrieve their satchel.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Tales remain of a Galaxy Expedition Team member
who boasted that he could increase the capacity<U+0010><U+0001>븀
of satchels so they could hold more items.

Potato Mochi<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Food prepared in Hisui by cooking sootfoot roots,
which could be harvested in Hisui at the time.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A recipe has even been found in writings from
the period:<U+0010><U+0001>븁
“Sootfoot, humble root—harvest it, and peel it.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
“Broiled, baked, or steamed will do, just let
nobody steal it.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
“Mash the root, then knead the mash, then once
more heat it over.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
“Grill it only till it browns—use Ember, not
Flamethrower.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
“Now hearken well, and listen closely—the wise
adore potato mochi.”

Life Around Jubilife<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Within the settlement of Jubilife, fields were
established to grow crops. Beyond its walls was<U+0010><U+0001>븀
the beach where settlers first came ashore.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
As more Pokémon were surveyed and the area
was developed, so too did the population grow.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is said that the Pokémon they befriended also
helped with various tasks, such as farming.

Model Reproduction of the General Store<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The general store is believed to have played a
central role in providing supplies to the settlers.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
There are records of other enterprises as well,
such as a clothier and a photography studio.

Survey Corps Uniform<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This uniform remained undamaged even when its
wearer rolled over rough terrain to dodge attacks<U+0010><U+0001>븀
from wild Pokémon.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It could withstand both heat and cold and is said
to have even withstood Pokémon moves.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Remarkably, the red cap is believed to have always
stayed in place, no matter how the wearer moved.

Survey Corps Uniform<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This uniform remained undamaged even when its
wearer rolled over rough terrain to dodge attacks<U+0010><U+0001>븀
from wild Pokémon.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It could withstand both heat and cold and is said
to have even withstood Pokémon moves.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Remarkably, the white kerchief was believed to
never slip off, no matter how the wearer moved.

The Training Grounds<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A space where Galaxy Expedition Team members
honed their skills for battling using Pokémon they<U+0010><U+0001>븀
had caught.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is worth noting that wild Pokémon were still
regarded as terrifying creatures at the time.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
There are records of a man named Ingo providing
guidance in the ways of Pokémon battle, but it is<U+0010><U+0001>븀
said that he simply vanished one day after stating,<U+0010><U+0001>븀
“It’s time for me to return.”

Shop Interiors<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Above is shown the interior of the hairdresser,
while below is the interior of the clothier.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
While life in Hisui is often regarded as one of
scarcity, residents were able to live in relative<U+0010><U+0001>븀
comfort by befriending Pokémon, as well as by<U+0010><U+0001>븀
using gathered materials to craft items.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The hairdresser also seemed to host salons, with
some residents gathering to play a game known<U+0010><U+0001>븀
as “Go” at the establishment.

House Interior<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Here is the interior of a standard house in the
early settlement of Jubilife.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Though sparsely furnished, it contains everything
needed for fieldwork and daily life, including<U+0010><U+0001>븀
hardy clothing, sandals, and boots.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Some houses also contained items the residents
brought with them from their home regions.

Hairstyles of the Time<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Displayed here are hairstyles said to have been
available at the hairdresser in Jubilife, the early<U+0010><U+0001>븀
settlement home to the Galaxy Expedition Team.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is also said that changing one’s hair color was
possible at this establishment.

Venerated Portraits<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Portraits said to have been displayed by the Pearl
Clan and Diamond Clan.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The individuals depicted within them are said to
have represented the sun, sea, and land, but<U+0010><U+0001>븀
nothing concrete is known about their identities.

Ancient Sinnoh Hieroglyphs<U+0010><U+0001>븁
These hieroglyphs were used in ancient Sinnoh
and are said to depict both common Pokémon<U+0010><U+0001>븀
and those that were objects of worship.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Each glyph held multiple meanings, and they
could be combined to create whole sentences.

“Almighty Sinnoh”<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A statue depicting the Spatial Pokémon Palkia,
worshiped by a group known as the Pearl Clan.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
They referred to it as almighty Sinnoh, the creator
of the entire world.

“Almighty Sinnoh”<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A statue depicting the Temporal Pokémon Dialga,
worshiped by a group called the Diamond Clan.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
They referred to it as almighty Sinnoh, the creator
of the entire world.

Formal Attire<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This outfit is said to have been worn by the
ancient Sinnoh people during their rituals.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
This group worshiped the Pokémon Arceus as an
almighty deity.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is thought that they showed their respect by
mimicking Arceus’s appearance—even reflected<U+0010><U+0001>븀
in the way that they styled their hair.

Temple of Sinnoh<U+0010><U+0001>븁
An artist’s rendition of what the ruins known as
the Spear Pillar would look like if restored.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is said that these ruins once housed 10 statues
depicting Pokémon known as lords or ladies.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
However, the temple was severely damaged due to
a battle between Legendary Pokémon, with the<U+0010><U+0001>븀
statues also being destroyed.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Records show that the name “Spear Pillar” was
coined by the Survey Corps of the time.

The Commander’s Armor<U+0010><U+0001>븁
A suit of armor worn in battle by Kamado, the
first commander of the Galaxy Expedition Team.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
It is said to have come from the Galar region and
bears a strong resemblance to the armor worn by<U+0010><U+0001>븀
Wikstrom, an Elite Four member of the Kalos<U+0010><U+0001>븀
region’s Pokémon League.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
When contacted for comment, Wikstrom said it
was possible this armor was one of several suits<U+0010><U+0001>븀
his ancestors gave to Galarians.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
However, it is difficult to verify such claims, given
relations between Kalos and Galar during the era.

Kimono<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Recreation of a kimono worn by Kamado, first
commander of the Galaxy Expedition Team.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The kimono uses many different types of thread
and is ornately decorated, showing that much<U+0010><U+0001>븀
effort was put into its creation.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Thus it is assumed the kimono was quite costly,
but it is unknown whether Kamado acquired it<U+0010><U+0001>븀
himself or if it was given to him as a gift.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The pattern provides evidence that Golduck could
be found at the time the cloth was embroidered.

Galaxy Expedition Team Flag<U+0010><U+0001>븁
One story claims that this flag was meant to show
that the Galaxy Team was made up of people from<U+0010><U+0001>븀
different regions, and so its design incorporates<U+0010><U+0001>븀
various elements, including Galarian letters.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
However, the truth of this tale remains unknown.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The flag itself seems to have been made using
threads from Pokémon.

The Ancient Quarry<U+0010><U+0001>븁
As its name would suggest, this cave was used in
ancient times as a stone quarry.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
The clean cuts on the rock surfaces are signs of
advanced techniques or possibly skilled command<U+0010><U+0001>븀
of Pokémon.<U+0010><U+0001>븁
Either way, the results are impressive even in this
modern age.
